revised: 13.4  Return or Destruction. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement, or upon request by the transferring Party, the Recipient shall promptly return or destroy (and certify such destruction in writing) all Biological Materials provided by the transferring Party, except to the extent retention is required by applicable law or regulation. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Recipient may retain: (a) specimens required to be retained under FDA or USDA regulation, solely for the period required by that regulation or until the applicable Regulatory Authority releases the retention requirement, whichever occurs first; and (b) longitudinal specimens with documented ongoing scientific research value, solely until the documented research purpose concludes. Within thirty (30) days after expiration or termination, the Recipient shall deliver to the transferring Party a written inventory of all retained specimens identifying the applicable regulatory or scientific basis for retention, the expected end date or triggering event for each retention category, the chain of custody, and the applicable biosafety classification. The Recipient shall provide quarterly written reports regarding all specimens retained for scientific preservation, including the continuing research purpose and anticipated end date, and shall destroy those specimens within thirty (30) days after the documented research purpose concludes. No retention under this Section may be open-ended, and the Recipient shall maintain chain-of-custody and biosafety-classification documentation for anything retained.
